title: Prompt injection against an AI agent (toy model)
root_cause: A language model receives developer instructions, user requests and untrusted content in one undifferentiated stream of text, so text inside a web page or email can be obeyed as an instruction. It is the same family as SQL injection (data interpreted as commands) in a new interpreter. This demo uses a deliberately naive rule-based stand-in for a model; it illustrates the architecture, it does not run or test any real LLM.
defenses: Give each agent task only the tools it needs (least privilege); a summarizer should not be able to send email.
Require human confirmation for sensitive or irreversible actions.
Enforce allow-lists (recipients, domains, file paths) in code outside the model.
Keep untrusted content clearly separated and never let it widen the agent's permissions.
Treat model-side filtering as a mitigation that reduces risk, not a guarantee.
